subject: Post-signature MAP and embedded implementation plan — next steps & canary windows
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@crestline.com>, John Patel <john.patel@crestline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-signature MAP and embedded implementation plan — next steps & canary windows

Samantha / John —

Thanks again for completing the paperwork — welcome aboard. Attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP_Crestline_v1.xlsx) and a short evaluation plan summary that embeds the implementation milestones (rollout, canary, migration, training). High-level asks from our side:

- Confirm internal owners for acceptance & security evidence (names + email) so we can pre-seed the checklist.
- Confirm which week you prefer for the initial canary (we propose two options below).
- Any hard blackout dates for May–June (we’ll avoid scheduled canaries during those windows).

Proposed canary windows (pick one):
- Option A: week of May 11 — 2-day canary (low-traffic slice) with smoke tests and 24h stability gate.
- Option B: week of May 18 — 3-day canary with extended load validation and training cutover.

What the attachments contain: MAP_Crestline_v1.xlsx — phased milestones, owners, risk gates, rollback criteria.
EvalPlan_Summary.pdf — short-run eval prompts, metric targets (latency P95, error rate, token cost variance), and acceptance thresholds.

We’ve cc’d Marissa (on implementation) and Ben (customer success/training) — they’ll lead the day-to-day delivery. If that looks good I’ll ask Marissa to publish a stabilized MAP and push calendar invites for the chosen canary.

Cheers,

Kimberly Park
Sr. Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Crestline_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), EvalPlan_Summary.pdf (one-page), Canary_Schedule.ics (stub)

From: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@crestline.com>

Date: Mon, 27 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-signature MAP and embedded implementation plan — next steps & canary windows

Kimberly — thanks and great to be moving. Quick responses below: 

- Owners: I’ll be primary acceptance owner (Samantha Reed). I’ll add our security liaison, John (cc’d) for SOC2 and evidence items.
- Canary week: Option B (week of May 18) is better for us — we have a client-facing release the week of May 4 and would prefer a later window.
- On migration duration: can you clarify whether the migration requires a blue/green cutover or incremental traffic shift? We prefer a gradual shift if possible.

Also, procurement flagged a standard procurement hold for KMS/HSM integration until we review key rotation docs. Can you point us to the SOC2 artifact and a short KMS integration note?

Appreciate the attachments — will review and circle back with any redlines by EOD Wednesday.

Best,
Samantha
Director, Platform Integrations
Crestline Health Systems

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@crestline.com>, John Patel <john.patel@crestline.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Revised MAP + canary cadence (embedded implementation plan)

Samantha / John —

Thanks — I updated the MAP with a multiphase execution sequence and a clearer set of risk gates. See attached "Crestline_MAP_v1.xlsx" (tab names: Overview, PhasePlan, RiskGates, Owners) and a downloadable calendar file (Canary_Schedule.ics). Key changes and clarifications below: 

Phase 0 — Preparation (May 4–15)
- Deliverables: infra provisioning, KMS/KV exchange, baseline performance run.
- Owners: Kimberly (CS), Ben (training), Crestline Sec (John).
- Gate: successful baseline run within 20% of expected P95 latency and infra health checks green.

Phase 1 — Canary (week of May 18)
- Window: May 18–20 (proposed, flexible).
- Traffic slice: 1–5% production traffic; auto-scale metrics enabled.
- Acceptance: zero P1 errors, <2% token cost variance, and human-eval pass rate >= 90% for selected prompts.
- Rollback criteria: sustained error rate >0.5% for 30m or P95 latency >2x baseline for 15m.

Phase 2 — Staged Migration (May 25–June 5)
- Gradual ramp (5% → 25% → 50% → 100%) with hold points and 24–48h stability checks.
- Training: concurrent trainer sessions during low-traffic windows; Ben to schedule 3 x 45-minute sessions (admin & ops).

Phase 3 — Full Cutover & Handover (June 8–12)
- Final acceptance sign-off, handover doc, and 30-day elevated support window.

Security/procurement note: John — attached EvalPlan_Summary.pdf includes the SOC2 pointer and a one-page KMS integration note. If your procurement needs additional artifacts we can escalate to our security team for direct transfer.

Next steps (action items):
- Samantha: confirm canary window (May 18–20) and list of 2–3 prompt sets for human eval.
- John: confirm security contact for evidence transfer and whether KMS/HSM needs a specific vendor form.
- Ben: will publish training invites once canary dates are finalized.

If everyone agrees I’ll publish a final MAP (v1.1) and send invites for the prep calls next Wednesday.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Manager, Implementation Services
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Crestline_MAP_v1.xlsx (updated), EvalPlan_Summary.pdf, Canary_Schedule.ics

From: John Patel <john.patel@crestline.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Marissa / Kimberly —

Thanks, this looks good. We approve Option B (May 18–20) for the canary. Gradual traffic shift is preferred (staged migration) — we do not want a single cutover. 

Procurement: I’ll send our security contact (Anita Shah) and a short list of required artifacts by EOD tomorrow — SOC2 report, KMS key rotation notes, and an encryption architecture diagram. If you have a short SLA/credits escalation page for latency regressions that would help the procurement review.

Kimberly — please schedule the prep call for May 7 and include our security lead. Ben — happy to make time for the training sessions.

John
SVP, Technical Operations
Crestline Health Systems
